title: Protein Representation Learning by Geometric Structure Pretraining
layout_note: Three titled columns divided by dotted vertical rules, read left to right. Protein Graph Construction: a stick model of a residue chain with the residue centres circled in black, a large hollow down arrow, then the numbered residue graph with coloured edges and an edge-type legend box. Spatial Relational Graph Neural Network: a dashed inset of node 4 and its neighbours, below it one row per edge type whose neighbour features pass a per-type step and are summed into node 4. Edge Message Passing: the same layout one level up, with edges as nodes labelled (i,j) and their messages summed into edge (4,7).
grouping: Edge type is the single colour key: blue sequential (d=1), yellow sequential (d=-1), red k-nearest-neighbour, green radius, given once in a rounded legend in the first column and reused for the graph's arrows, the row frames, the tinted bars and the curved arrows in the other two columns. Dashed rounded insets hold the local neighbourhood being updated.
shapes_depth: Flat: numbered grey-outlined circles for residues; in the edge column, rounded tinted rectangles labelled (i,j) stand for edges. Feature vectors are small upright bars - black-outlined grey for inputs, tinted in the edge-type colour after the per-relation step - and a circle-plus sums the rows into one output bar. Curved coloured arrows; the input is a rendered stick model with green carbons.
proposed_highlight: No 'ours' highlight; the two modules are the titled second and third columns, and the relational idea is shown by giving every edge type its own row and colour.
lesson: Fix one colour per edge type in the graph-construction panel and reuse it for the per-relation rows of the message-passing panels, so the reader can follow sequential, radius and kNN edges from the protein to the aggregation.
notes: Venue and year from the PDF first page ('Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2023'; venue_source: pdf). The whole figure is one embedded raster in the PDF, so photo_share is null.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.task: protein structure representation (relational GNN with edge message passing)
taxonomy.note: paradigm: relational GCN (R-GCN) style message passing

core.what: A protein residue chain becomes a numbered graph with coloured edge types, and the relational update is drawn on that graph: node 4's neighbourhood (dashed inset) is split into one row per edge type, each row's features passed through its own weight and summed into node 4.

relations.form: three titled columns left to right separated by dotted rules: graph construction, node-level relational GNN, edge-level message passing
column 1: a stick model with circled residue centres, a hollow block arrow down to a 7-node graph whose directed edges are coloured by type
columns 2 and 3 each start with a dashed inset of the local neighbourhood (node 4; edge (4,7) in a line graph) taken from the graph
below each inset, one coloured row per relation (feature bars in a frame -> a coloured weight bar), curved coloured arrows converging on one circled-plus and the output bar
column 3 repeats column 2's row-and-sum skeleton one level up, with edges as nodes

channels.colour: edge type, keyed once in the legend (blue / yellow sequential, red kNN, green radius) and reused for graph arrows, row frames and weight bars in column 2; column 3's row frames and arrows switch to orange, blue, black and purple, which are not in the legend, so colour changes meaning between columns
channels.shape: numbered circle = residue node, rounded labelled box = edge-as-node, dark bar = feature vector, tinted bar = relation-specific weight, circled plus = sum
channels.line: coloured arrows = typed messages, hollow block arrow = construction step, dotted vertical rules = column dividers
channels.frame: dashed rounded box = local neighbourhood inset; coloured rectangle = features grouped by relation

quality.strengths: The relational aggregation is drawn as geometry: one row per edge type with its own weight, converging on one sum, under the neighbourhood it comes from; the edge-type colour key is taught once and carried from graph arrows into rows; columns 2 and 3 share a skeleton so the edge-level extension reads as the same operation one level up.
quality.weaknesses: Column 3's colours (orange, purple, black) are unkeyed and conflict with column 2's edge-type meaning; the converging arrows are long curves that cross; the stick model in column 1 is small and the circled residues are hard to map to graph node numbers.

insights.structure: Three titled columns divided by dotted vertical rules: protein graph construction, the relational GNN update of node 4, and the same update one level up for edge (4,7).
insights.data: A real stick model of a residue chain with circled residue centres sits top-left; the graph is numbered nodes with coloured directed edges, and features are small dark bars inside coloured frames.
insights.emphasis: Edge type is the single colour key (blue/yellow sequential, red kNN, green radius) given once in a rounded legend and reused for arrows, row frames and per-type weight bars.
insights.flow: Down within column 1 via a large hollow arrow, then left-to-right in columns 2-3 where each row's per-type transform curves into a circled-plus sum on the right.
insights.avoid: Column 3 recolours edge types (orange, purple, black) that the column-1 legend does not define.

arrangement.units: three columns titled at top and separated by dotted rules; each method column has a dashed rounded inset of the local neighbourhood above per-type rows
arrangement.inputs_as: 3-D stick render of the protein in the top-left
arrangement.shared: edge-type colour key across all columns
